# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1229
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1229
- **Title**: gh-1199 [GOAL] Deterministic-only Quality gate: mock LLM everywhere, live models move to supervised benches
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1199` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1157
- **Deletions**: -99
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T14:06:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T16:17:37Z

## PR Description

### What changed

Deterministic-only Quality gate (gh-1199): the per-PR integration shards now exclude every `llm`-tagged file at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), a lint enforces the tag boundary forever, the full suite is audited mock-vs-live, and a flake quarantine + hourly watcher catch the next #1171. Live models keep their supervised home (tag-only provider smoke, nightly, benches).

### Key decisions

- **AC1**: `shard_files.py`/`assert_shard_manifest.py` grew `--exclude-tag` (manifest units + runtime bin-packs both filtered); red/green proof is `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` running the exact CI invocation.
- **AC2**: `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` — heuristic lint (real provider URL; credential-key literal without a mock/loopback marker), scoped to integration-tagged files, pinned `AUDIT_MOCK` list; wired into the static gate + the regular test suite. Result: 9 live, 2 pinned, 0 violations.
- **AC3/E4**: the live-wire codex boot leg moved out of `poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart` into `provider_codex_boot_live_test.dart` (`llm`); `fa_llm_mock_config_test`'s flake-prone fallback-queue leg is now scenario-routed on a unique marker + sticky taggen wildcard (fallback queue serve/exhaust stays unit-covered in `packages/fa_llm_mock`).
- **AC4**: sticky-wildcard mock contract + `memory_taggen_script_pin_test.dart` REG pin were already landed — kept and documented; no rewrite.
- **AC5**: rule documented in AGENTS.md quality-gates section + new `docs/live-llm-testing.md` (gate vs benches, boundary table, quarantine semantics).
- **AC6**: `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR) + `apply_quarantine.py` (gate legs pipe targets through it; `--check` guards the list in the static gate) + `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml`/`flake_watch.py` (≥2 distinct-SHA reds in 24h → `flake`-labelled issue with run evidence + quarantine PR). Nightly deliberately does NOT quarantine — it produces the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.

### How to verify

```bash
python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py
python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm
dart test test/scripts/ test/integration/fa_llm_mock_config_test.dart
```

# gh-1199: [GOAL] Deterministic-only Quality gate: mock LLM everywhere, live models move to supervised benches

## Description

## Goal — the Quality gate is deterministic-only: mock LLM everywhere, live models live in the benches

One sentence: **the merge-blocking Quality gate runs exclusively on mock LLMs — every live-provider test is excluded from the gate by an enforced `llm` tag boundary — and real-model verification happens in the bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) run under supervision, so a model's mood never blocks a merge again.**

## Owner's framing (2026-10-03)

«Я ожидаю что у нас там будет mock llm использоваться везде… для реальных тестов у нас бенчи есть, и их мы будем запускать под присмотром.» The gate answers «did this PR break the code»; benches answer «does the agent work against real models today». Never mix the two questions in one red/green signal.

## Evidence — today's failures are one class, not N regressions

Failing Quality-gate legs sampled across 6 recent failed ci.yml runs (2026-10-03):

| Run / PR | Failing test | Root cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 37131299118 / PR #1173, shard 0/3 | `provider_ollama_test`: expected `add`, actual `add<\|channel\|>commentary` | **live Ollama Cloud model changed its chat-template output** — the model's drift, not the PR |
| 37128386208, shard 1/3 | `subagent_integration_test` memory_add timeout (30s waiting «✔ memory_add») | **#1171 — mock-script exhaustion** (see below) |
| 37127519520, shard 1/3 | same test, same timeout | #1171 again — twice in one day |
| 37131131303, shard 1/3 | `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback queue: expected «fallback reply», actual «» | mock-config integration flake — same audit |
| parked PRs #1163/#1165 | kicker head-completeness / sm-liveness | machine-infra guards, not code |

The machine digest said it precisely: «гостевой контент валит статик-гейты — чинить должны авторы» — except the authors CAN'T fix model drift; the gate must stop asking live models questions.

## #1171 in full detail (the recurring offender, folded into this card)

**Test**: `test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart: memory_add and memory_search tools are available`, `@Tags(['integration','pty'])`, runs a real CLI in a PTY with a **scripted mock LLM**.
**Mechanism**: the mock serves a fixed script of responses. The memory feature's **auto-tagging** inserted an EXTRA LLM call (screen dump: «Existing tags: … Query: \"Dart\"», «Do NOT invent tags…») that the test's script doesn't account for; when scheduling shifts, the script runs dry → `[net] connection lost (500: {"error":{"message":"mock: script exhausted after 7 …` → the CLI dies mid-test → `TimeoutException … waiting for "✔ memory_add"` (30s).
**Proof of flakiness, not regression**: main @ 389bd86 green at 16:19Z, red at 16:33Z — same SHA; PR #1162 head failed with this exact error, `gh run rerun --failed` → green with zero code changes. Seen repeatedly: 36895063649 (10-01), 37128386208, 37127519520 (10-03).
**Owner's expectation**: this class must not exist — either the mock harness tolerates incidental calls by construction, or the test disables auto-tagging deterministically.

## The two boundary leaks (why live/brittle tests reach the gate at all)

- **Leak 1 — the gate doesn't honor the `llm` tag**: integration shards select via `scripts/shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext` — `llm` is NOT excluded, so with `OLLAMA_API_KEY` present in CI the live ollama suite executes in the merge-blocking gate. The tag's documented intent (`--exclude-tags llm`, manual `--tags "integration && llm"`) is real; the gate just ignores it.
- **Leak 2 — tag discipline is unenforced**: tests that spend mock-script calls against incidental features (#1171's auto-tag) or hit live endpoints can be added with only `integration`/`pty` tags and silently join the gate. Nothing fails when a live-touching file lacks `llm`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — Gate excludes live**: the Quality-gate integration shard selection adds `--exclude llm` (or `--exclude-tags llm` at the dart-test invocation, per shard); a red/green proof: the ollama suite no longer appears in gate shard listings (`shard_files.py` dry-run output asserted in a workflow test).
- **AC2 — Tag boundary enforced forever**: a CI lint (script + gate step) fails the Quality gate when a test file that performs live provider I/O (heuristic: imports provider config/env keys like `*_API_KEY` env reads, real baseUrl usage — the audit list is pinned in the PR) lacks the `llm` tag. New live tests can never leak again («раз и навсегда»).
- **AC3 — Full audit lands**: every existing test file classified `mock` (gate) or `live` (`llm` tag); the two known leaks resolved: `provider_ollama_test` (already `llm` — now excluded by AC1) and `fa_llm_mock_config_test`'s live-fallback case (mocked deterministically or tagged `llm`).
- **AC4 — #1171 fixed at the harness level**: the scripted-mock library gains an explicit contract for incidental calls — EITHER a wildcard/overflow response class («script exhausted» becomes a served stub, never a 500), OR the test pins auto-tagging off; whichever is chosen, the memory integration test is green **10/10 consecutive CI runs** (repeat-run proof job, one-off).
- **AC5 — Live suite has a supervised home**: docs (AGENTS.md testing section + docs/) state the rule — live-LLM verification runs via the bench harnesses under supervision (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench), manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging; NO scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path.
- **AC6 — Flake safety net**: same test red in ≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h → the machine auto-files/updates a flake issue AND the test is skipped in the gate pending the fix (quarantine list checked in, reviewed in the fix PR). This catches the NEXT #1171 before it parks five PRs.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — A PR that legitimately ADDS a live test: the lint (AC2) blocks the merge until tagged `llm`; the PR body checklist mentions it.
- **E2** — `llm`-tagged tests still compile/parse in the gate (they're excluded from RUN, not from `dart analyze`) — no dead-code rot; a scheduled weekly compile-check keeps them loadable.
- **E3** — Quarantine (AC6) must never swallow a REAL regression: a quarantined test's issue carries the failing runs; un-quarantine requires the repeat-run proof from AC4.
- **E4** — `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback case: if the empty reply came from the MOCK config path itself (not live), it stays in the gate but gets the same deterministic-script treatment as AC4.

## Non-goals
No changes to the bench harnesses themselves (they already run supervised); no rewrite of the mock-LLM library beyond the AC4 contract; no reduction of unit-test coverage (mocks cover the same assertions, minus the network).

## References
- #1171 (the flake, full history folded in above); failing runs 37131299118, 37128386208, 37127519520, 37131131303 (2026-10-03); machine digest «Парк красных вырос до 5».
- Gate shard selection: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext`; manual live path documented in `provider_ollama_test.dart` header.
- Bench supervision framing: bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml / bench-mls.yml (#1124, #1161).

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37206417212) · started 13:41 · done 14:06 ✅

  "key": "gh-1199",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Deterministic-only Quality gate: mock LLM everywhere, live models move to supervised benches",
    "description": "## Goal — the Quality gate is deterministic-only: mock LLM everywhere, live models live in the benches

One sentence: **the merge-blocking Quality gate runs exclusively on mock LLMs — every live-provider test is excluded from the gate by an enforced `llm` tag boundary — and real-model verification happens in the bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) run under supervision, so a model's mood never blocks a merge again.**

## Owner's framing (2026-10-03)

«Я ожидаю что у нас там будет mock llm использоваться везде… для реальных тестов у нас бенчи есть, и их мы будем запускать под присмотром.» The gate answers «did this PR break the code»; benches answer «does the agent work against real models today». Never mix the two questions in one red/green signal.

## Evidence — today's failures are one class, not N regressions

Failing Quality-gate legs sampled across 6 recent failed ci.yml runs (2026-10-03):

| Run / PR | Failing test | Root cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 37131299118 / PR #1173, shard 0/3 | `provider_ollama_test`: expected `add`, actual `add<\|channel\|>commentary` | **live Ollama Cloud model changed its chat-template output** — the model's drift, not the PR |
| 37128386208, shard 1/3 | `subagent_integration_test` memory_add timeout (30s waiting «✔ memory_add») | **#1171 — mock-script exhaustion** (see below) |
| 37127519520, shard 1/3 | same test, same timeout | #1171 again — twice in one day |
| 37131131303, shard 1/3 | `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback queue: expected «fallback reply», actual «» | mock-config integration flake — same audit |
| parked PRs #1163/#1165 | kicker head-completeness / sm-liveness | machine-infra guards, not code |

The machine digest said it precisely: «гостевой контент валит статик-гейты — чинить должны авторы» — except the authors CAN'T fix model drift; the gate must stop asking live models questions.

## #1171 in full detail (the recurring offender, folded into this card)

**Test**: `test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart: memory_add and memory_search tools are available`, `@Tags(['integration','pty'])`, runs a real CLI in a PTY with a **scripted mock LLM**.
**Mechanism**: the mock serves a fixed script of responses. The memory feature's **auto-tagging** inserted an EXTRA LLM call (screen dump: «Existing tags: … Query: \"Dart\"», «Do NOT invent tags…») that the test's script doesn't account for; when scheduling shifts, the script runs dry → `[net] connection lost (500: {"error":{"message":"mock: script exhausted after 7 …` → the CLI dies mid-test → `TimeoutException … waiting for "✔ memory_add"` (30s).
**Proof of flakiness, not regression**: main @ 389bd86 green at 16:19Z, red at 16:33Z — same SHA; PR #1162 head failed with this exact error, `gh run rerun --failed` → green with zero code changes. Seen repeatedly: 36895063649 (10-01), 37128386208, 37127519520 (10-03).
**Owner's expectation**: this class must not exist — either the mock harness tolerates incidental calls by construction, or the test disables auto-tagging deterministically.

## The two boundary leaks (why live/brittle tests reach the gate at all)

- **Leak 1 — the gate doesn't honor the `llm` tag**: integration shards select via `scripts/shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext` — `llm` is NOT excluded, so with `OLLAMA_API_KEY` present in CI the live ollama suite executes in the merge-blocking gate. The tag's documented intent (`--exclude-tags llm`, manual `--tags "integration && llm"`) is real; the gate just ignores it.
- **Leak 2 — tag discipline is unenforced**: tests that spend mock-script calls against incidental features (#1171's auto-tag) or hit live endpoints can be added with only `integration`/`pty` tags and silently join the gate. Nothing fails when a live-touching file lacks `llm`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — Gate excludes live**: the Quality-gate integration shard selection adds `--exclude llm` (or `--exclude-tags llm` at the dart-test invocation, per shard); a red/green proof: the ollama suite no longer appears in gate shard listings (`shard_files.py` dry-run output asserted in a workflow test).
- **AC2 — Tag boundary enforced forever**: a CI lint (script + gate step) fails the Quality gate when a test file that performs live provider I/O (heuristic: imports provider config/env keys like `*_API_KEY` env reads, real baseUrl usage — the audit list is pinned in the PR) lacks the `llm` tag. New live tests can never leak again («раз и навсегда»).
- **AC3 — Full audit lands**: every existing test file classified `mock` (gate) or `live` (`llm` tag); the two known leaks resolved: `provider_ollama_test` (already `llm` — now excluded by AC1) and `fa_llm_mock_config_test`'s live-fallback case (mocked deterministically or tagged `llm`).
- **AC4 — #1171 fixed at the harness level**: the scripted-mock library gains an explicit contract for incidental calls — EITHER a wildcard/overflow response class («script exhausted» becomes a served stub, never a 500), OR the test pins auto-tagging off; whichever is chosen, the memory integration test is green **10/10 consecutive CI runs** (repeat-run proof job, one-off).
- **AC5 — Live suite has a supervised home**: docs (AGENTS.md testing section + docs/) state the rule — live-LLM verification runs via the bench harnesses under supervision (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench), manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging; NO scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path.
- **AC6 — Flake safety net**: same test red in ≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h → the machine auto-files/updates a flake issue AND the test is skipped in the gate pending the fix (quarantine list checked in, reviewed in the fix PR). This catches the NEXT #1171 before it parks five PRs.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — A PR that legitimately ADDS a live test: the lint (AC2) blocks the merge until tagged `llm`; the PR body checklist mentions it.
- **E2** — `llm`-tagged tests still compile/parse in the gate (they're excluded from RUN, not from `dart analyze`) — no dead-code rot; a scheduled weekly compile-check keeps them loadable.
- **E3** — Quarantine (AC6) must never swallow a REAL regression: a quarantined test's issue carries the failing runs; un-quarantine requires the repeat-run proof from AC4.
- **E4** — `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback case: if the empty reply came from the MOCK config path itself (not live), it stays in the gate but gets the same deterministic-script treatment as AC4.

## Non-goals
No changes to the bench harnesses themselves (they already run supervised); no rewrite of the mock-LLM library beyond the AC4 contract; no reduction of unit-test coverage (mocks cover the same assertions, minus the network).

## References
- #1171 (the flake, full history folded in above); failing runs 37131299118, 37128386208, 37127519520, 37131131303 (2026-10-03); machine digest «Парк красных вырос до 5».
- Gate shard selection: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext`; manual live path documented in `provider_ollama_test.dart` header.
- Bench supervision framing: bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml / bench-mls.yml (#1124, #1161).

- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37206417212) · started 13:41 · done 14:06 ✅"

  js-ext-integration:
    name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Install quickjs-ng
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs" \
            https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs/releases/download/v0.16.2/qjs-linux-x86_64
          chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: dart test --tags integration (qjs engine suites)
        run: dart test --tags integration test/cli/ext_engine_process_test.dart test/js_ext/integration/

  publish:
    name: Publish to pub.dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [quality-gate, integration]
    # 20m ceiling: publish flow (~2-4m) + the post-upload verify window
    # (11m, #611) must both fit — 10m would kill a healthy poll mid-window.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check — the fa#456 class: GitHub propagates
    # "skipped" TRANSITIVELY through the always()-quality-gate's needs graph.
    # Path-gated legs (perf-gate is PR-only) skip on EVERY tag run, so this
    # job's implicit success() condition force-skipped publish on every tag
    # since the gate graph grew — quality-gate showed green, publish never
    # ran, and pub.dev stalled at v0.1.369 for 35 releases (#554). Same fix
    # pattern as the release/integration/binaries jobs. The release arm
    # covers tags that only ever fire a release event (the v0.1.370-402 era:
    # API-created lightweight tags produce no push event, so publish never
    # even triggered there).
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:

# PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions

The Binaries smoke gate is an aggregation over binaries-pr matrix — the actual build failures could be on any OS. The JS engine integration runs `dart test --tags integration test/cli/ext_engine_process_test.dart test/js_ext/integration/`.

To reproduce the load condition, I could run it concurrently with other PTY tests from shard 2. That mimics the CI leg. Let me run the exact shard 2 invocation but maybe just a subset. The full shard 2 has 29 files and takes very long. Alternatively run dap_wake_hang concurrently with the heaviest PTY neighbors.

Actually, first let me check git history — has dap_wake_hang_test changed recently? And was the wedge timeout (15s marker wait) a recent change? Also check how long the test took in my local run vs CI (90.5s on main CI).

Let me also think about the failed CI run more: the failing run 37214807813 started shard 2 at 15:55:34, the test failed at 15:58:08 — so dap_wake_hang ran early in the shard (probably first, given it failed at ~2.5 min into the job while other tests show timestamps after 15:58:28). Wait, actually looking at the passing tests list, tests passed after 15:58:28. The dap_wake_hang test started right after boot at 15:57:14 (session file name 15-57-14). So it ran FIRST in the shard. Hmm, so concurrency load from shard-mates wasn't the cause — it ran at the start, possibly concurrently with dart compile/pub of the other suites... Actually dart test compiles all suites first.

The marker "Ответ #14." — the session shows the answer WAS generated at 15:57:30. Then 38s of status-bar repaint without rendering the transcript. That's a genuine wedge in the CLI TUI (the exact class the test hunts: a wake turn that never finishes painting / spinner stuck). But ESC was sent after the 15s timeout, then dump, then fail. Interesting: after ESC + 500ms settle, the screen STILL showed only the status bar.

Could this be a real product wedge exposed by... the PR doesn't touch product code. Not PR-caused. It's the known flaky PTY class. Single red.

Per the PR's own AC6 design and the quarantine list's own rules ("runs: the gate run ids that proved the flake, >=2 distinct SHAs"), a single red cannot be quarantined. So the correct handling: fix the deterministic pin failure (done), and for dap_wake_hang — since the owner directive says "red yields the slot", a re-run after the fix push is expected. But should I harden the test anyway?

Let me look at what the machine has done in similar cases — the quarantine list previously had theme_readability (fa#1205) with documented runs. Let me check git log for test_quarantine.json to see the entry that was removed... Actually the current file has empty quarantined list. The theme_readability skip came from QUARANTINE marker in dart test skip — different mechanism (in-file skip). 

Options for dap_wake_hang:
1. Leave as-is, note as flake in response.md (CI re-run will likely pass — it passed twice on main with the same parent).
2. Harden the test: e.g., the wedge forensics show the answer arrived; the test could verify the wedge is real vs render-lag. Modifying this test is risky and out of PR scope.

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider whether the PR's shard rebalance made dap_wake_hang run FIRST. In the old shard 2, files were listed alphabetically with dap_wake_hang at position 10. Tests run alphabetically by path within the shard invocation? dart test runs suites in the order given, with concurrency 4. So dap_wake_hang started early in both cases. Fine.

One more angle: the failing CI run was on ubuntu-24.04-arm. My local run is x64. The arm runner may be slower. The test does `await Future.delayed(2s)` between DMs; marker timeout 15s.

Given the constraints, my call: treat dap_wake_hang as a non-PR-caused timing flake; do NOT modify it (out of scope, and a "fix" without root cause would be noise). Document it in response.md. The push of the pin fix creates a NEW head which re-runs CI — per the owner directive, a new head gets a fresh validation.

Hmm, but wait — the instructions say "Fix CI root cause". The root causes of the 4 failed checks:
- Binaries smoke gate → artifact of dynamic bookkeeping run (no steps, no logs) — will clear on new head.
- JS engine integration → same.
- Quality gate ×2 → (a) pin typo (fixed), (b) dap_wake_hang flake.

Actually, let me look more carefully — is it possible the "dynamic" run 37214532892 is a checks-rerun where the merge bot re-requested failed checks, and GitHub created jobs with no steps? The Binaries smoke gate job completed in 0 seconds with failure. These are synthetic. The REAL binaries-pr job in the main CI run was "skipped" because... event was workflow_dispatch/push, not pull_request. OK whatever — they're artifacts.

Let me now double-check there are no other instances of the wrong SHA anywhere else, and run the full PR verification steps:
1. python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py ✅ (ran, 0 violations)
2. assert_shard_manifest ✅
3. dart test/scripts/ test/integration/fa_llm_mock_config_test.dart

Also check flake_watch.py / apply_quarantine.py --check. And review the workflows for yaml syntax validity (flake-watch.yml is new). Let me run the repo's own workflow-shape tests if any.
Passes locally — consistent with a load/timing flake on the arm runner, not PR-caused. Let me verify there are no other stray SHA pins and run the PR's full verification suite.

# gh-1199: [GOAL] Deterministic-only Quality gate: mock LLM everywhere, live models move to supervised benches

## Description

## Goal — the Quality gate is deterministic-only: mock LLM everywhere, live models live in the benches

One sentence: **the merge-blocking Quality gate runs exclusively on mock LLMs — every live-provider test is excluded from the gate by an enforced `llm` tag boundary — and real-model verification happens in the bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) run under supervision, so a model's mood never blocks a merge again.**

## Owner's framing (2026-10-03)

«Я ожидаю что у нас там будет mock llm использоваться везде… для реальных тестов у нас бенчи есть, и их мы будем запускать под присмотром.» The gate answers «did this PR break the code»; benches answer «does the agent work against real models today». Never mix the two questions in one red/green signal.

## Evidence — today's failures are one class, not N regressions

Failing Quality-gate legs sampled across 6 recent failed ci.yml runs (2026-10-03):

| Run / PR | Failing test | Root cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 37131299118 / PR #1173, shard 0/3 | `provider_ollama_test`: expected `add`, actual `add<\|channel\|>commentary` | **live Ollama Cloud model changed its chat-template output** — the model's drift, not the PR |
| 37128386208, shard 1/3 | `subagent_integration_test` memory_add timeout (30s waiting «✔ memory_add») | **#1171 — mock-script exhaustion** (see below) |
| 37127519520, shard 1/3 | same test, same timeout | #1171 again — twice in one day |
| 37131131303, shard 1/3 | `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback queue: expected «fallback reply», actual «» | mock-config integration flake — same audit |
| parked PRs #1163/#1165 | kicker head-completeness / sm-liveness | machine-infra guards, not code |

The machine digest said it precisely: «гостевой контент валит статик-гейты — чинить должны авторы» — except the authors CAN'T fix model drift; the gate must stop asking live models questions.

## #1171 in full detail (the recurring offender, folded into this card)

**Test**: `test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart: memory_add and memory_search tools are available`, `@Tags(['integration','pty'])`, runs a real CLI in a PTY with a **scripted mock LLM**.
**Mechanism**: the mock serves a fixed script of responses. The memory feature's **auto-tagging** inserted an EXTRA LLM call (screen dump: «Existing tags: … Query: \"Dart\"», «Do NOT invent tags…») that the test's script doesn't account for; when scheduling shifts, the script runs dry → `[net] connection lost (500: {"error":{"message":"mock: script exhausted after 7 …` → the CLI dies mid-test → `TimeoutException … waiting for "✔ memory_add"` (30s).
**Proof of flakiness, not regression**: main @ 389bd86 green at 16:19Z, red at 16:33Z — same SHA; PR #1162 head failed with this exact error, `gh run rerun --failed` → green with zero code changes. Seen repeatedly: 36895063649 (10-01), 37128386208, 37127519520 (10-03).
**Owner's expectation**: this class must not exist — either the mock harness tolerates incidental calls by construction, or the test disables auto-tagging deterministically.

## The two boundary leaks (why live/brittle tests reach the gate at all)

- **Leak 1 — the gate doesn't honor the `llm` tag**: integration shards select via `scripts/shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext` — `llm` is NOT excluded, so with `OLLAMA_API_KEY` present in CI the live ollama suite executes in the merge-blocking gate. The tag's documented intent (`--exclude-tags llm`, manual `--tags "integration && llm"`) is real; the gate just ignores it.
- **Leak 2 — tag discipline is unenforced**: tests that spend mock-script calls against incidental features (#1171's auto-tag) or hit live endpoints can be added with only `integration`/`pty` tags and silently join the gate. Nothing fails when a live-touching file lacks `llm`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — Gate excludes live**: the Quality-gate integration shard selection adds `--exclude llm` (or `--exclude-tags llm` at the dart-test invocation, per shard); a red/green proof: the ollama suite no longer appears in gate shard listings (`shard_files.py` dry-run output asserted in a workflow test).
- **AC2 — Tag boundary enforced forever**: a CI lint (script + gate step) fails the Quality gate when a test file that performs live provider I/O (heuristic: imports provider config/env keys like `*_API_KEY` env reads, real baseUrl usage — the audit list is pinned in the PR) lacks the `llm` tag. New live tests can never leak again («раз и навсегда»).
- **AC3 — Full audit lands**: every existing test file classified `mock` (gate) or `live` (`llm` tag); the two known leaks resolved: `provider_ollama_test` (already `llm` — now excluded by AC1) and `fa_llm_mock_config_test`'s live-fallback case (mocked deterministically or tagged `llm`).
- **AC4 — #1171 fixed at the harness level**: the scripted-mock library gains an explicit contract for incidental calls — EITHER a wildcard/overflow response class («script exhausted» becomes a served stub, never a 500), OR the test pins auto-tagging off; whichever is chosen, the memory integration test is green **10/10 consecutive CI runs** (repeat-run proof job, one-off).
- **AC5 — Live suite has a supervised home**: docs (AGENTS.md testing section + docs/) state the rule — live-LLM verification runs via the bench harnesses under supervision (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench), manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging; NO scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path.
- **AC6 — Flake safety net**: same test red in ≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h → the machine auto-files/updates a flake issue AND the test is skipped in the gate pending the fix (quarantine list checked in, reviewed in the fix PR). This catches the NEXT #1171 before it parks five PRs.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — A PR that legitimately ADDS a live test: the lint (AC2) blocks the merge until tagged `llm`; the PR body checklist mentions it.
- **E2** — `llm`-tagged tests still compile/parse in the gate (they're excluded from RUN, not from `dart analyze`) — no dead-code rot; a scheduled weekly compile-check keeps them loadable.
- **E3** — Quarantine (AC6) must never swallow a REAL regression: a quarantined test's issue carries the failing runs; un-quarantine requires the repeat-run proof from AC4.
- **E4** — `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback case: if the empty reply came from the MOCK config path itself (not live), it stays in the gate but gets the same deterministic-script treatment as AC4.

## Non-goals
No changes to the bench harnesses themselves (they already run supervised); no rewrite of the mock-LLM library beyond the AC4 contract; no reduction of unit-test coverage (mocks cover the same assertions, minus the network).

## References
- #1171 (the flake, full history folded in above); failing runs 37131299118, 37128386208, 37127519520, 37131131303 (2026-10-03); machine digest «Парк красных вырос до 5».
- Gate shard selection: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext`; manual live path documented in `provider_ollama_test.dart` header.
- Bench supervision framing: bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml / bench-mls.yml (#1124, #1161).

- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37206417212) · started 13:41 · done 14:06 ✅

«Я ожидаю что у нас там будет mock llm использоваться везде… для реальных тестов у нас бенчи есть, и их мы будем запускать под присмотром.» The gate answers «did this PR break the code»; benches answer «does the agent work against real models today». Never mix the two questions in one red/green signal.

## Evidence — today's failures are one class, not N regressions

Failing Quality-gate legs sampled across 6 recent failed ci.yml runs (2026-10-03):

| Run / PR | Failing test | Root cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 37131299118 / PR #1173, shard 0/3 | `provider_ollama_test`: expected `add`, actual `add<\|channel\|>commentary` | **live Ollama Cloud model changed its chat-template output** — the model's drift, not the PR |
| 37128386208, shard 1/3 | `subagent_integration_test` memory_add timeout (30s waiting «✔ memory_add») | **#1171 — mock-script exhaustion** (see below) |
| 37127519520, shard 1/3 | same test, same timeout | #1171 again — twice in one day |
| 37131131303, shard 1/3 | `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback queue: expected «fallback reply», actual «» | mock-config integration flake — same audit |
| parked PRs #1163/#1165 | kicker head-completeness / sm-liveness | machine-infra guards, not code |

The machine digest said it precisely: «гостевой контент валит статик-гейты — чинить должны авторы» — except the authors CAN'T fix model drift; the gate must stop asking live models questions.

## #1171 in full detail (the recurring offender, folded into this card)

**Test**: `test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart: memory_add and memory_search tools are available`, `@Tags(['integration','pty'])`, runs a real CLI in a PTY with a **scripted mock LLM**.
**Mechanism**: the mock serves a fixed script of responses. The memory feature's **auto-tagging** inserted an EXTRA LLM call (screen dump: «Existing tags: … Query: \"Dart\"», «Do NOT invent tags…») that the test's script doesn't account for; when scheduling shifts, the script runs dry → `[net] connection lost (500: {"error":{"message":"mock: script exhausted after 7 …` → the CLI dies mid-test → `TimeoutException … waiting for "✔ memory_add"` (30s).
**Proof of flakiness, not regression**: main @ 389bd86 green at 16:19Z, red at 16:33Z — same SHA; PR #1162 head failed with this exact error, `gh run rerun --failed` → green with zero code changes. Seen repeatedly: 36895063649 (10-01), 37128386208, 37127519520 (10-03).
**Owner's expectation**: this class must not exist — either the mock harness tolerates incidental calls by construction, or the test disables auto-tagging deterministically.

## The two boundary leaks (why live/brittle tests reach the gate at all)

- **Leak 1 — the gate doesn't honor the `llm` tag**: integration shards select via `scripts/shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext` — `llm` is NOT excluded, so with `OLLAMA_API_KEY` present in CI the live ollama suite executes in the merge-blocking gate. The tag's documented intent (`--exclude-tags llm`, manual `--tags "integration && llm"`) is real; the gate just ignores it.
- **Leak 2 — tag discipline is unenforced**: tests that spend mock-script calls against incidental features (#1171's auto-tag) or hit live endpoints can be added with only `integration`/`pty` tags and silently join the gate. Nothing fails when a live-touching file lacks `llm`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — Gate excludes live**: the Quality-gate integration shard selection adds `--exclude llm` (or `--exclude-tags llm` at the dart-test invocation, per shard); a red/green proof: the ollama suite no longer appears in gate shard listings (`shard_files.py` dry-run output asserted in a workflow test).
- **AC2 — Tag boundary enforced forever**: a CI lint (script + gate step) fails the Quality gate when a test file that performs live provider I/O (heuristic: imports provider config/env keys like `*_API_KEY` env reads, real baseUrl usage — the audit list is pinned in the PR) lacks the `llm` tag. New live tests can never leak again («раз и навсегда»).
- **AC3 — Full audit lands**: every existing test file classified `mock` (gate) or `live` (`llm` tag); the two known leaks resolved: `provider_ollama_test` (already `llm` — now excluded by AC1) and `fa_llm_mock_config_test`'s live-fallback case (mocked deterministically or tagged `llm`).
- **AC4 — #1171 fixed at the harness level**: the scripted-mock library gains an explicit contract for incidental calls — EITHER a wildcard/overflow response class («script exhausted» becomes a served stub, never a 500), OR the test pins auto-tagging off; whichever is chosen, the memory integration test is green **10/10 consecutive CI runs** (repeat-run proof job, one-off).
- **AC5 — Live suite has a supervised home**: docs (AGENTS.md testing section + docs/) state the rule — live-LLM verification runs via the bench harnesses under supervision (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench), manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging; NO scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path.
- **AC6 — Flake safety net**: same test red in ≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h → the machine auto-files/updates a flake issue AND the test is skipped in the gate pending the fix (quarantine list checked in, reviewed in the fix PR). This catches the NEXT #1171 before it parks five PRs.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — A PR that legitimately ADDS a live test: the lint (AC2) blocks the merge until tagged `llm`; the PR body checklist mentions it.
- **E2** — `llm`-tagged tests still compile/parse in the gate (they're excluded from RUN, not from `dart analyze`) — no dead-code rot; a scheduled weekly compile-check keeps them loadable.
- **E3** — Quarantine (AC6) must never swallow a REAL regression: a quarantined test's issue carries the failing runs; un-quarantine requires the repeat-run proof from AC4.
- **E4** — `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback case: if the empty reply came from the MOCK config path itself (not live), it stays in the gate but gets the same deterministic-script treatment as AC4.

## Non-goals
No changes to the bench harnesses themselves (they already run supervised); no rewrite of the mock-LLM library beyond the AC4 contract; no reduction of unit-test coverage (mocks cover the same assertions, minus the network).

## References
- #1171 (the flake, full history folded in above); failing runs 37131299118, 37128386208, 37127519520, 37131131303 (2026-10-03); machine digest «Парк красных вырос до 5».
- Gate shard selection: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext`; manual live path documented in `provider_ollama_test.dart` header.
- Bench supervision framing: bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml / bench-mls.yml (#1124, #1161).

  js-ext-integration:
    name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Install quickjs-ng
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs" \
            https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs/releases/download/v0.16.2/qjs-linux-x86_64
          chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: dart test --tags integration (qjs engine suites)
        run: dart test --tags integration test/cli/ext_engine_process_test.dart test/js_ext/integration/

  publish:
    name: Publish to pub.dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [quality-gate, integration]
    # 20m ceiling: publish flow (~2-4m) + the post-upload verify window
    # (11m, #611) must both fit — 10m would kill a healthy poll mid-window.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check — the fa#456 class: GitHub propagates
    # "skipped" TRANSITIVELY through the always()-quality-gate's needs graph.
    # Path-gated legs (perf-gate is PR-only) skip on EVERY tag run, so this
    # job's implicit success() condition force-skipped publish on every tag
    # since the gate graph grew — quality-gate showed green, publish never
    # ran, and pub.dev stalled at v0.1.369 for 35 releases (#554). Same fix
    # pattern as the release/integration/binaries jobs. The release arm
    # covers tags that only ever fire a release event (the v0.1.370-402 era:
    # API-created lightweight tags produce no push event, so publish never
    # even triggered there).
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:

blocks.text:
# PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix

## PR Description

### What changed

Deterministic-only Quality gate (gh-1199): the per-PR integration shards now exclude every `llm`-tagged file at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), a lint enforces the tag boundary forever, the full suite is audited mock-vs-live, and a flake quarantine + hourly watcher catch the next #1171. Live models keep their supervised home (tag-only provider smoke, nightly, benches).

### Key decisions

- **AC1**: `shard_files.py`/`assert_shard_manifest.py` grew `--exclude-tag` (manifest units + runtime bin-packs both filtered); red/green proof is `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` running the exact CI invocation.

- **AC5**: rule documented in AGENTS.md quality-gates section + new `docs/live-llm-testing.md` (gate vs benches, boundary table, quarantine semantics).

```bash
python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py
python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

# gh-1199: [GOAL] Deterministic-only Quality gate: mock LLM everywhere, live models move to supervised benches

## Description

## Goal — the Quality gate is deterministic-only: mock LLM everywhere, live models live in the benches

One sentence: **the merge-blocking Quality gate runs exclusively on mock LLMs — every live-provider test is excluded from the gate by an enforced `llm` tag boundary — and real-model verification happens in the bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) run under supervision, so a model's mood never blocks a merge again.**

## Owner's framing (2026-10-03)

«Я ожидаю что у нас там будет mock llm использоваться везде… для реальных тестов у нас бенчи есть, и их мы будем запускать под присмотром.» The gate answers «did this PR break the code»; benches answer «does the agent work against real models today». Never mix the two questions in one red/green signal.

## Evidence — today's failures are one class, not N regressions

Failing Quality-gate legs sampled across 6 recent failed ci.yml runs (2026-10-03):

| Run / PR | Failing test | Root cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 37131299118 / PR #1173, shard 0/3 | `provider_ollama_test`: expected `add`, actual `add<\|channel\|>commentary` | **live Ollama Cloud model changed its chat-template output** — the model's drift, not the PR |
| 37128386208, shard 1/3 | `subagent_integration_test` memory_add timeout (30s waiting «✔ memory_add») | **#1171 — mock-script exhaustion** (see below) |
| 37127519520, shard 1/3 | same test, same timeout | #1171 again — twice in one day |
| 37131131303, shard 1/3 | `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback queue: expected «fallback reply», actual «» | mock-config integration flake — same audit |
| parked PRs #1163/#1165 | kicker head-completeness / sm-liveness | machine-infra guards, not code |

The machine digest said it precisely: «гостевой контент валит статик-гейты — чинить должны авторы» — except the authors CAN'T fix model drift; the gate must stop asking live models questions.

## #1171 in full detail (the recurring offender, folded into this card)

**Test**: `test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart: memory_add and memory_search tools are available`, `@Tags(['integration','pty'])`, runs a real CLI in a PTY with a **scripted mock LLM**.
**Mechanism**: the mock serves a fixed script of responses. The memory feature's **auto-tagging** inserted an EXTRA LLM call (screen dump: «Existing tags: … Query: \"Dart\"», «Do NOT invent tags…») that the test's script doesn't account for; when scheduling shifts, the script runs dry → `[net] connection lost (500: {"error":{"message":"mock: script exhausted after 7 …` → the CLI dies mid-test → `TimeoutException … waiting for "✔ memory_add"` (30s).
**Proof of flakiness, not regression**: main @ 389bd86 green at 16:19Z, red at 16:33Z — same SHA; PR #1162 head failed with this exact error, `gh run rerun --failed` → green with zero code changes. Seen repeatedly: 36895063649 (10-01), 37128386208, 37127519520 (10-03).
**Owner's expectation**: this class must not exist — either the mock harness tolerates incidental calls by construction, or the test disables auto-tagging deterministically.

## The two boundary leaks (why live/brittle tests reach the gate at all)

- **Leak 1 — the gate doesn't honor the `llm` tag**: integration shards select via `scripts/shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext` — `llm` is NOT excluded, so with `OLLAMA_API_KEY` present in CI the live ollama suite executes in the merge-blocking gate. The tag's documented intent (`--exclude-tags llm`, manual `--tags "integration && llm"`) is real; the gate just ignores it.
- **Leak 2 — tag discipline is unenforced**: tests that spend mock-script calls against incidental features (#1171's auto-tag) or hit live endpoints can be added with only `integration`/`pty` tags and silently join the gate. Nothing fails when a live-touching file lacks `llm`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — Gate excludes live**: the Quality-gate integration shard selection adds `--exclude llm` (or `--exclude-tags llm` at the dart-test invocation, per shard); a red/green proof: the ollama suite no longer appears in gate shard listings (`shard_files.py` dry-run output asserted in a workflow test).
- **AC2 — Tag boundary enforced forever**: a CI lint (script + gate step) fails the Quality gate when a test file that performs live provider I/O (heuristic: imports provider config/env keys like `*_API_KEY` env reads, real baseUrl usage — the audit list is pinned in the PR) lacks the `llm` tag. New live tests can never leak again («раз и навсегда»).
- **AC3 — Full audit lands**: every existing test file classified `mock` (gate) or `live` (`llm` tag); the two known leaks resolved: `provider_ollama_test` (already `llm` — now excluded by AC1) and `fa_llm_mock_config_test`'s live-fallback case (mocked deterministically or tagged `llm`).
- **AC4 — #1171 fixed at the harness level**: the scripted-mock library gains an explicit contract for incidental calls — EITHER a wildcard/overflow response class («script exhausted» becomes a served stub, never a 500), OR the test pins auto-tagging off; whichever is chosen, the memory integration test is green **10/10 consecutive CI runs** (repeat-run proof job, one-off).
- **AC5 — Live suite has a supervised home**: docs (AGENTS.md testing section + docs/) state the rule — live-LLM verification runs via the bench harnesses under supervision (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench), manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging; NO scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path.
- **AC6 — Flake safety net**: same test red in ≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h → the machine auto-files/updates a flake issue AND the test is skipped in the gate pending the fix (quarantine list checked in, reviewed in the fix PR). This catches the NEXT #1171 before it parks five PRs.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — A PR that legitimately ADDS a live test: the lint (AC2) blocks the merge until tagged `llm`; the PR body checklist mentions it.
- **E2** — `llm`-tagged tests still compile/parse in the gate (they're excluded from RUN, not from `dart analyze`) — no dead-code rot; a scheduled weekly compile-check keeps them loadable.
- **E3** — Quarantine (AC6) must never swallow a REAL regression: a quarantined test's issue carries the failing runs; un-quarantine requires the repeat-run proof from AC4.
- **E4** — `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback case: if the empty reply came from the MOCK config path itself (not live), it stays in the gate but gets the same deterministic-script treatment as AC4.

## Non-goals
No changes to the bench harnesses themselves (they already run supervised); no rewrite of the mock-LLM library beyond the AC4 contract; no reduction of unit-test coverage (mocks cover the same assertions, minus the network).

## References
- #1171 (the flake, full history folded in above); failing runs 37131299118, 37128386208, 37127519520, 37131131303 (2026-10-03); machine digest «Парк красных вырос до 5».
- Gate shard selection: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext`; manual live path documented in `provider_ollama_test.dart` header.
- Bench supervision framing: bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml / bench-mls.yml (#1124, #1161).

- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37206417212) · started 13:41 · done 14:06 ✅

    "summary": "[GOAL] Deterministic-only Quality gate: mock LLM everywhere, live models move to supervised benches",
    "description": "## Goal — the Quality gate is deterministic-only: mock LLM everywhere, live models live in the benches

One sentence: **the merge-blocking Quality gate runs exclusively on mock LLMs — every live-provider test is excluded from the gate by an enforced `llm` tag boundary — and real-model verification happens in the bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) run under supervision, so a model's mood never blocks a merge again.**

## Owner's framing (2026-10-03)

«Я ожидаю что у нас там будет mock llm использоваться везде… для реальных тестов у нас бенчи есть, и их мы будем запускать под присмотром.» The gate answers «did this PR break the code»; benches answer «does the agent work against real models today». Never mix the two questions in one red/green signal.

## Evidence — today's failures are one class, not N regressions

Failing Quality-gate legs sampled across 6 recent failed ci.yml runs (2026-10-03):

| Run / PR | Failing test | Root cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 37131299118 / PR #1173, shard 0/3 | `provider_ollama_test`: expected `add`, actual `add<\|channel\|>commentary` | **live Ollama Cloud model changed its chat-template output** — the model's drift, not the PR |
| 37128386208, shard 1/3 | `subagent_integration_test` memory_add timeout (30s waiting «✔ memory_add») | **#1171 — mock-script exhaustion** (see below) |
| 37127519520, shard 1/3 | same test, same timeout | #1171 again — twice in one day |
| 37131131303, shard 1/3 | `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback queue: expected «fallback reply», actual «» | mock-config integration flake — same audit |
| parked PRs #1163/#1165 | kicker head-completeness / sm-liveness | machine-infra guards, not code |

The machine digest said it precisely: «гостевой контент валит статик-гейты — чинить должны авторы» — except the authors CAN'T fix model drift; the gate must stop asking live models questions.

## #1171 in full detail (the recurring offender, folded into this card)

**Test**: `test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart: memory_add and memory_search tools are available`, `@Tags(['integration','pty'])`, runs a real CLI in a PTY with a **scripted mock LLM**.
**Mechanism**: the mock serves a fixed script of responses. The memory feature's **auto-tagging** inserted an EXTRA LLM call (screen dump: «Existing tags: … Query: \"Dart\"», «Do NOT invent tags…») that the test's script doesn't account for; when scheduling shifts, the script runs dry → `[net] connection lost (500: {"error":{"message":"mock: script exhausted after 7 …` → the CLI dies mid-test → `TimeoutException … waiting for "✔ memory_add"` (30s).
**Proof of flakiness, not regression**: main @ 389bd86 green at 16:19Z, red at 16:33Z — same SHA; PR #1162 head failed with this exact error, `gh run rerun --failed` → green with zero code changes. Seen repeatedly: 36895063649 (10-01), 37128386208, 37127519520 (10-03).
**Owner's expectation**: this class must not exist — either the mock harness tolerates incidental calls by construction, or the test disables auto-tagging deterministically.

## The two boundary leaks (why live/brittle tests reach the gate at all)

- **Leak 1 — the gate doesn't honor the `llm` tag**: integration shards select via `scripts/shard_files.py … --tags integration --exclude browser_ext` — `llm` is NOT excluded, so with `OLLAMA_API_KEY` present in CI the live ollama suite executes in the merge-blocking gate. The tag's documented intent (`--exclude-tags llm`, manual `--tags "integration && llm"`) is real; the gate just ignores it.
- **Leak 2 — tag discipline is unenforced**: tests that spend mock-script calls against incidental features (#1171's auto-tag) or hit live endpoints can be added with only `integration`/`pty` tags and silently join the gate. Nothing fails when a live-touching file lacks `llm`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — Gate excludes live**: the Quality-gate integration shard selection adds `--exclude llm` (or `--exclude-tags llm` at the dart-test invocation, per shard); a red/green proof: the ollama suite no longer appears in gate shard listings (`shard_files.py` dry-run output asserted in a workflow test).
- **AC2 — Tag boundary enforced forever**: a CI lint (script + gate step) fails the Quality gate when a test file that performs live provider I/O (heuristic: imports provider config/env keys like `*_API_KEY` env reads, real baseUrl usage — the audit list is pinned in the PR) lacks the `llm` tag. New live tests can never leak again («раз и навсегда»).
- **AC3 — Full audit lands**: every existing test file classified `mock` (gate) or `live` (`llm` tag); the two known leaks resolved: `provider_ollama_test` (already `llm` — now excluded by AC1) and `fa_llm_mock_config_test`'s live-fallback case (mocked deterministically or tagged `llm`).
- **AC4 — #1171 fixed at the harness level**: the scripted-mock library gains an explicit contract for incidental calls — EITHER a wildcard/overflow response class («script exhausted» becomes a served stub, never a 500), OR the test pins auto-tagging off; whichever is chosen, the memory integration test is green **10/10 consecutive CI runs** (repeat-run proof job, one-off).
- **AC5 — Live suite has a supervised home**: docs (AGENTS.md testing section + docs/) state the rule — live-LLM verification runs via the bench harnesses under supervision (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench), manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging; NO scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path.
- **AC6 — Flake safety net**: same test red in ≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h → the machine auto-files/updates a flake issue AND the test is skipped in the gate pending the fix (quarantine list checked in, reviewed in the fix PR). This catches the NEXT #1171 before it parks five PRs.

### Edge cases
- **E1** — A PR that legitimately ADDS a live test: the lint (AC2) blocks the merge until tagged `llm`; the PR body checklist mentions it.
- **E2** — `llm`-tagged tests still compile/parse in the gate (they're excluded from RUN, not from `dart analyze`) — no dead-code rot; a scheduled weekly compile-check keeps them loadable.
- **E3** — Quarantine (AC6) must never swallow a REAL regression: a quarantined test's issue carries the failing runs; un-quarantine requires the repeat-run proof from AC4.
- **E4** — `fa_llm_mock_config_test` fallback case: if the empty reply came from the MOCK config path itself (not live), it stays in the gate but gets the same deterministic-script treatment as AC4.

## Non-goals
No changes to the bench harnesses themselves (they already run supervised); no rewrite of the mock-LLM library beyond the AC4 contract; no reduction of unit-test coverage (mocks cover the same assertions, minus the network).

## References
- #1171 (the flake, full history folded in above); failing runs 37131299118, 37128386208, 37127519520, 37131131303 (2026-10-03); machine digest «Парк красных вырос до 5».

- Bench supervision framing: bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml / bench-mls.yml (#1124, #1161).

  js-ext-integration:
    name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Install quickjs-ng
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs" \
            https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs/releases/download/v0.16.2/qjs-linux-x86_64
          chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: dart test --tags integration (qjs engine suites)
        run: dart test --tags integration test/cli/ext_engine_process_test.dart test/js_ext/integration/

  publish:
    name: Publish to pub.dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [quality-gate, integration]
    # 20m ceiling: publish flow (~2-4m) + the post-upload verify window
    # (11m, #611) must both fit — 10m would kill a healthy poll mid-window.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check — the fa#456 class: GitHub propagates
    # "skipped" TRANSITIVELY through the always()-quality-gate's needs graph.
    # Path-gated legs (perf-gate is PR-only) skip on EVERY tag run, so this
    # job's implicit success() condition force-skipped publish on every tag
    # since the gate graph grew — quality-gate showed green, publish never
    # ran, and pub.dev stalled at v0.1.369 for 35 releases (#554). Same fix
    # pattern as the release/integration/binaries jobs. The release arm
    # covers tags that only ever fire a release event (the v0.1.370-402 era:
    # API-created lightweight tags produce no push event, so publish never
    # even triggered there).
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:

blocks.text:
# PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
